I ran a small social services business with the goal of simply covering our costs while helping people in our community. Unfortunately, we could no longer financially sustain it and had to close.

Yelp continued charging me for months afterward, leaving me personally responsible for nearly $1,400 in charges. When I contacted Customer Success, I was initially told I had never canceled and was asked to provide proof. Because the business had already closed and our email accounts had been deleted, I no longer had access to those records.

After pushing them to investigate further, Yelp confirmed that I had canceled my Page Upgrades, but then told me that their records also show my advertising budget nearly tripled on that exact same day. It makes absolutely no sense that a business in the process of shutting down would intentionally cancel & triple the budget in the same day.

My experience with Yelp's advertising and cancellation process has been incredibly shady, the Customer Success team has been misleading and not supportive. After this experience, I cannot recommend Yelp to other small business owners at all.

I am filing this complaint regarding Yelp’s review filtering practices and the impact they are having on my business.

Our business currently has approximately 37 five-star customer reviews that Yelp has placed in the “not recommended” section. These reviews appear to be from legitimate customers who used our services and took the time to share their experiences. However, Yelp does not include these reviews in our displayed rating, making them difficult for potential customers to find.

This creates a misleading impression of our business and does not accurately represent the feedback we have received from our customers. Yelp does not provide a clear explanation of why each review was removed from the recommended section, nor does it provide a meaningful appeal process for the business owner or reviewer.

I understand that Yelp uses automated software to identify potentially unreliable reviews. However, when dozens of legitimate five-star reviews are excluded, the system appears unfair, inaccurate, and damaging to the reputation of the business.

I am requesting that Yelp:

1. Conduct a manual review of the 37 five-star reviews currently marked as “not recommended.”
2. Provide a specific explanation for why each review was filtered.
3. Restore any reviews that were submitted by verified, legitimate customers.
4. Provide a fair and transparent appeal process for businesses affected by review filtering.
5. Correct our displayed rating to accurately reflect all legitimate customer feedback.

These reviews directly affect consumer perception, search visibility, and our ability to compete fairly. Businesses should not be financially or reputationally harmed by an automated system without transparency, accountability, or a reasonable opportunity to challenge inaccurate decisions.

I am requesting a written response explaining what Yelp will do to investigate and resolve this issue.

text:
My Experience With Yelp Advertising – A Warning for Small Business Owners

I am sharing my experience so other small business owners can make informed decisions before signing up for Yelp advertising services.

I was contacted by a Yelp representative and was assisted with setting up an advertising account. During this process, I provided payment information. However, I was never provided a contract by mail, never received a signed agreement, and, to the best of my knowledge, was never emailed any advertising agreement or terms and conditions.

Yelp offered promotional advertising credits as part of the account setup. During the advertising period, I began receiving messages that I believed were not resulting in legitimate business opportunities. In several instances, messages would be received, but after responding, there was no further communication. This raised concerns for me regarding the quality of the leads being generated.

Because of these concerns, I made the decision to cancel my Yelp advertising account. I have documentation showing that the account was canceled, and Yelp’s own records acknowledge the cancellation date.

Despite the cancellation, I was later charged $863. I disputed the charge and attempted to resolve the matter directly with Yelp. Unfortunately, I was unable to obtain a satisfactory resolution through customer service.

I subsequently filed a complaint with my state’s Attorney General’s office. Yelp responded to the Attorney General’s inquiry, but I remained dissatisfied with the company’s position and explanation regarding the charges.

Throughout this process, I repeatedly requested clarification regarding the basis for the charges and any agreement authorizing them. My concern remains that I was charged after cancellation despite my understanding that the account had already been terminated.

I encourage any small business owner considering Yelp advertising to:

• Carefully review all advertising terms and conditions.
• Request copies of any agreements in writing.
• Save all emails, account records, and cancellation confirmations.
• Monitor billing statements closely.
• Document all communications with representatives.
• Keep records of cancellation dates and account activity.

This post reflects my personal experience and opinions based on my records and interactions. Other business owners may have different experiences. I encourage everyone to conduct their own research and maintain thorough documentation when entering into any advertising agreement.

Business Owner,
TTR TAX & NOTARY CO LLC
title: My Experience With Yelp Advertising

text:
I am beyond frustrated with Yelp and the way they handle serious issues that directly damage a business’s reputation.

We recently received a negative review from someone who clearly confused our company with another business. This is not the first time — it has happened multiple times. Every time, we report it, explain the situation, and provide context. And every single time, Yelp did absolutely nothing.

This is unacceptable. Incorrect reviews are not harmless — they lower our rating, mislead potential clients, and directly impact our revenue. A platform that profits from businesses should have basic systems in place to verify or remove clearly inaccurate reviews. Yelp chooses not to.

What makes this even worse is the constant pressure to pay for advertising. Yelp has no problem calling, emailing, and pushing for higher monthly payments, yet shows zero urgency when it comes to protecting the businesses that fund their platform.

At this point, it feels like Yelp is more interested in selling visibility than maintaining fairness or accuracy. There is a clear lack of accountability, transparency, and real support.

For any business considering relying on Yelp, be aware: you may be paying to be on a platform that allows false information to harm your reputation — and does nothing to fix it.
title: Lack of Accountability and Support for Businesses

text: My husband and I have eaten at Pha Khao in Racine, WI several times, and enjoyed it. During previous visits, the service was good. This time, it was the opposite. We arrived with another couple for an early dinner, but all the tables were full. The owner did not greet us, nor did he say how long we'd have to wait. Looking tense, he told a couple of teenage girls in black to vacate a table for four, and began cleaning it. The girls went behind the bar and began laughing and talking loudly. The owner gestured us to the table and we sat down, then he served water. Another teenaged girl appeared to take our drink orders. She looked grumpy, and was dressed in an overlarge t-shirt, baggy pajama bottoms, and what looked like bedroom scuffs. My husband tried to tease a smile from her, but she only lifted the corners of her mouth. The owner came out to verify my choice of Chateau Ste. The grumpy teen came back for our food orders: my husband chose Crisp Noodles with Chicken, and I asked for Shrimp and Basil Noodles. She entered our choices on a handheld machine, and left. The teens who were making noise behind the bar finally disappeared. Our food came in a reasonable time, except for my Shrimp and Basil Noodles, which somehow had turned into Shrimp Fried Rice. I refused that dish, and told the teen what I'd originally ordered. The owner came over, and I told him what had happened. He took the Shrimp Fried Rice back to the kitchen and put in my original order. It was served by the woman who was cooking, who had waited on us during a previous visit. The food was delicious. text:
We gave Yelp every reason to work with us. A complete, polished profile. High-quality photos. Detailed service descriptions. Regular posts. Full case studies documenting our real work for real clients. We responded to every message. We even spent $1,000 on Yelp ads, because we wanted to do things properly.

Then, without warning, Yelp moved two legitimate 5-star reviews into their "Not Recommended" section—effectively hiding them from the public entirely.

These weren't throwaway reviews. They were detailed, genuine testimonials from verified customers. One reviewer posted video footage of the completed job. We built complete case studies around both projects. By any reasonable standard, these were exactly the kind of reviews a consumer platform should want to surface.

But here's where it gets difficult to accept: Yelp's official position is that they didn't remove anything. The reviews are technically still there. They're just hidden from everyone who visits your profile. That distinction—between "hidden" and "deleted"—may protect Yelp legally. In practice, the effect on your business is identical. Your credibility disappears overnight, with no warning and no explanation.

When we reached out to support, we were told it was "the algorithm." No escalation path. No appeals team. No resolution. Just a shrug wrapped in policy language.

Think about what that actually means for small business owners. You can invest months of effort, deliver outstanding work, earn genuine praise from real customers—and a platform's opaque automated system can silently erase that social proof while you're none the wiser. And when you ask why? There's no one there to answer.

Yelp frames this as consumer protection. But hiding authentic feedback from real customers doesn't protect consumers. It misleads them—while simultaneously punishing the businesses that earned those reviews fairly.

To any small business owner reading this: build your reputation on ground that won't shift beneath you. Your own website, your own testimonials, your own channels—places where your work speaks for itself without a third party deciding whether it deserves to be seen. If a platform profits from your ad spend while quietly undermining your credibility, the most rational response is to stop funding it. Redirect that budget somewhere your effort is actually rewarded.

If you absolutely need a third party resource, I'd go with a Google Business Profile and any number of social media platforms before ever considering Yelp.
title: 1★ — Yelp quietly buried our reputation.

Beteendet från vakten kan betraktas som relativt oförskämt och opassande, särskilt med tanke på din artighet, klädsel och dyra accessoar. Här är en analys av situationen på en skala från 1 till 10, där 1 är normalt och 10 är fullkomligt oacceptabelt:

3. **Insisterande på att du skulle dricka något (skala 6-7)**: Att vakten fortsätter att fråga vad du ska dricka efter att du tydligt sagt att du inte dricker alkohol kan verka tjatigt och respektlöst.

4. **Sammanlagd upplevelse (skala 7-8)**: Sammantaget, med tanke på att du var artig, välklädd och erbjöd tydliga förklaringar, känns vakten överdrivet misstänksam och oförskämd. Din upplevelse som helhet kan därmed bedömas som högre på skalan.

Sammanfattningsvis, vakten uppvisade ett beteende som jag skulle placera på en skala mellan 7 och 8, där 1 är normalt och 10 är fullkomligt oacceptabelt. Det betyder att vakten var ganska oförskämd och det kunde hanterats mer respektfullt och professionellt.

J'ai récemment fait appel à "Casa Menuiserie" (13270 Fos-sur-Mer) pour l'installation d'une porte moustiquaire avec cadre en aluminium de chez MARITON, équipée d'une toile "air métal" en fils alu tissés.

La commerciale de "Casa Menuiserie" m'a présenté le fournisseur MARITON comme l'un des meilleurs du marché avec des produits de haute qualité.

- La première fois, la toile n'était pas correctement tendue.
- La deuxième fois, la toile était déchirée (photo ci-jointe).
- La troisième fois, après la pose définitive et paiement du solde, j'ai constaté que la toile était légèrement gondolée sur la partie basse et l'un des bords du cadre présentait des mailles abîmées (photo ci-jointe).

De plus, lors de la pose du cadre en aluminium, "Casa Menuiserie" a endommagé le cadre de ma porte d'entrée en éclatant un gros morceau de crépi (photo ci-jointe).

La société n'a pas fait appel à un maçon pour réparer les dégâts. Le crépi a été sommairement réparé par le menuisier, qui n'est pas du métier.
J'ai donc dû procéder moi-même aux finitions, notamment la peinture de l'encadrement.

Pour une prestation qui m'a coûté 1585 euros TTC (pose comprise), je m'attendais à une qualité et un service bien supérieurs.
Je suis très déçu et ne recommande pas ces entreprises.

text:
Leaf Filter and Gutter Guard Company - Virginia Beach
My elderly mother-in-law lives in Virginia Beach, My wife (her daughter) and I live in Myrtle Beach. We make at least one trip to Virginia every 5 weeks to visit with her and to take care of business she needs assistance with. Unfortunately, we can’t oversee every aspect of her day-to-day life. We have found that there is no shortage of unscrupulous vultures, all to eager to take advantage of the elderly.
One establishment charged her $900 to replace a car battery, saying the expense was because they had to take the front right tire off the car to access the battery compartment. Most oil change businesses rotate all four tires as part of the service. They don’t charge $3,600 to remove four tires.
Last week, she called Mike Horan of Leaf Filter Gutter Protection Company to provide a quote for gutter guards. He gave her a fair price. She couldn’t explain it to me over the phone so I called Mike. He explained it to me and even stated he had given her his employee discount because she was elderly and on a fixed income.
I’m the president of the HOA in our community and we are currently pricing gutter guards for our townhomes. I know that Mike gave her a great price. Withing two days, Mike’s team had installed the gutter guards, cleaned up after themselves and left without causing any unnecessary anxiety or extra follow-up. 
AT LAST!! An honest contractor!! Mike and his company certainly have my full and grateful endorsement.
title: Leaf Filter and Gutter Guard Company

text: I have shopped at Dollar General for many years. I always found it convenient and decent prices. When they closed the one on Pontiac Lake road in Waterford I switched to the one on Summit Drive in Waterford. I was a little nervous at first with all the reported break ins they had at the time but I still went. For a couple of years everything was adequate. However the place is really going down. The floors look like they havent been mopped in several years, nor the shelves wiped. Half the time the items I go in for (i.e. one of the two brands of water I get, coke, orange poweraide, Welches grape juice, Mac and cheese cups, and many more) are out of stock.  I dont know if this is because of shipping issues, the items not being ordered, or the fact that they seem to move at a snails pace unloading the supply carts that no matter what day you go in, are blocking most of the aisles making it difficult to move through the store.  The other thing I have had to watch out for is expired items on the shelf as it seems they do not check dates. Several weeks ago Jiff recalled its peanut butter for salmomilla. They pulled it off the shelves but I noticed several jars still on the overstock shelf. I mentioned this to a worker and two weeks later when I was back in the jars were still there. Makes me worry if they didnt just get shoved back on the shelf when the recall ended with the fresh peanut butter.  I will admit the workers are friendly, in some cases too friendly as they get into converstions with some customers at the checkout and slow the line down to a stop.  Stores like Dollar General are a convenience. The prices are usually a little lower, and you dont have to go into those big stores and deal with the self checkout nonsense. However when the convenience is no longer there, the product is no longer there, and it can be a risk to your health, I would just as soon go to a big box store like Meijer or Kroger.  Mind you this is not neccessarily all Dollar Generals, I can only speak for this one that I have used. Like I say the one that used to be on Pontiac Lake was nice.
title: Dollar General Waterford, two thumbs way down!!!

text:
· Just now  · 
Ok here is our "in Depth review" of Colts BBQ in downtown Prescott. By our calculations (there maybe others), there are basically three BBQ restaurants in Prescott area. Big Daddy E's in Chino Valley, Lucy D's in Prescott and Colts now in Prescott (and Colts has one in Prescott valley, Sedona and Cottonwood- you can get ribs at Hassayampa and Lone Spur). We ate lunch at Colts today (Saturday). Overall we rate it about a 6 out of 10. Kathy's burger was very good and well priced and large. (and messy to eat) My ribs were OK, slightly overcooked and arrived with BBQ sauce all over them rather than allowing me to choose one from their BBQ sauce collection and about 14 ribs for $26.00 (good price). Kathy had smoked Mac and Cheese and if you like smoked Mac and Cheese then you might like this Mac and Cheese (we did not). The cole slaw was average to less than average and "Bill's Grill" in Prescott has WAY better cole slaw.They have obviously put a lot on money into developing this restaurant and did a good job with what they had to work with lot size. BUT it is very long and narrow and other tables are fairly close by (I'd say the people are about 2 feet away from one another). Quite noisy as the area where they cook/prepare one's meal is open and approx 8 people working back there. When you walk in the menu is right by the door where you walk in and is on a blackboard on the wall with a "zillion" (exaggerating SLIGHTLY ) choices and one can be overwhelmed with choices as people are coming in behind you and "backing up" into the entrance (suggest reading the menu online before you go so you know what you want to order and don't have to hold up the other people backing up behind you and now out the door). VERY smokey INSIDE and when one leaves one smells like BBQ smoke (which some people may like and others may not). Nit picking here but the napkins are VERY thin and flimsy and if one is eating BBQ, one usually needs something akin to paper towels. Not a lot of instruction as to where one goes  to get one's food and the utensils are where one picks up their food, so best figure that out first because they YELL out your number to come get your food and low and behold there are the napkins (in one dispenser) and the utensils which you now do not have enough hands to carry everything back to one's table. The bathrooms are clean but again they need a different dispenser for paper towels after one washes their hands and you need about ten to dry your hands and they rip in half as you try to pull them out. When getting my diet coke, diet coke came out the bottom of the dispenser and water streamed out the top and all over my arm. I called an employee over and she took off the nozzle with her bare hand and then screwed it back on bare handed (gloves might have been better??) Obviously there is no onsite parking so when tourist season arrives, parking might be difficult to find but excellent location. Some of these items (all?) may be to "growing pains" and we shall see. We prefer Lucy D's more and rate Lucy's as an 8 out of ten. Quieter, more space between tables, quicker to get one's food, thick paper towels on the tables, and one doesn't smell like smoke when one leaves (On Sheldon ST.) and plenty of parking and outdoor picnic tables which I imagine Colts will have this Spring???? Big Daddy E's in Chino has excellent ribs and brisket, plenty of parking but weird hours it is open! We rate Big Daddy E's a 7 out of ten overall BUT crowded on a Friday night and small number of tables but Earl who owns it is a good guy and 20 year Navy Sub cook!!
title: Colt's BBQ Prescott, AZ

It is now Nov. 2021 and I have officially closed the book on going to this restaurant ever again. I can only hope they get their act together before they drive this place out of business.

text: It represents a story for interactions between consumer/respondent business before & after consumer feedback posting. But in fact, they censor feedback based not on actual filtering via Quality Control but rather when one of their whiney lil snitches overreacts to getting a bad review based on facts. Time and time again, they'd toss out negative reviews based on, "that does not fulfill our divine commitment to our Community Guidelines commandments from on high," as if they gave a hoot! The reality, some of these sleazy businesses pay them for advertising where no such operations are supported. So let's say you go into Hamburgers Galore, buy a burger, and find a booger inside. Before leaving counter, you're like talking to boogey distributor, "Jesusth Christh! Can you please explain how this got planted beneath my bun like omg!" Then, HG reluctantly offers a replacement burger or refund, so you're like refund me mudda effas. Here's the pickle that Yelp's HQ outta San Francisco will molest your backside with weeks after posting above factually. Instead of recognizing your place in above transaction, they prefer seeing paid digital "advertiser's" perspective, countering, Butt, you're not really a customer remember? To close, their slant includes a boiler room where their own customer base outweighs anything you may have to say regardless of how informative such a report may be. So this "bait & switch routine" described above enables Censors to call out reviews in hindsight like judge & Jury, no meaningful Appeal possible. As I pointed out, if you were truly interested in protecting Community Guidelines, then you'd call or message with specific reference to complainant's content, results of secondary evaluation, and so on and so forth. What you see by email judgment is smack that goes on about how not respecting CG forced their hand, "but go ahead , keep resubmitting and our same crew polishing that same Censor will put it through grinder again." Slanted censorship always pushes down honest feedback and tends to indemnify those who know someone on receiving end of their ad premiums paid. Yelp's mission, folks, was consumer insight for folks to find out which ones in their directory remain snakes all coiled up and hissing. But beware, Yelp curates feedback not as advertised. Others in market place who show off this doublespeak include BBB (regulating businesses outside US) , AMAZON , and eBay. The bigger they are, the more readily you will find them bent over for the ballers, not a consumers who is trying to point out you need to more carefully inspect what was bought or you may find something gross stuck in between your teeth. text: I have yet to have Bellhop provide the move, however, I want to post this review regarding the contracting and customer service. Be prepared for them to request monies earlier than told at the time of booking services, a 5% deposit (which they told me would be charged 2 days prior to the move) and the remaining balance, a few days prior to the move date (which they told me would be the day of the move).    This will put a hold on your money with your bank.   The due date for payments will be on the receipt they email you, they just don't use those dates.  Finally, be prepared to be hung up on when you call the company.  It took 3 calls to get through to the correct department and then, once I had the appropriate department on the line, they hung up on me when they did not like what I was saying.  This company came highly recommended by my daughter and I am surprised by the treatment thus far.  I am coordinating this small move from my brother, from a nursing home to an assisted living facility.  I do not live in the state he lives in and thought the recommendation and national presence of this company would work out.  If you are  looking for professional telephone service, this may not be the company for you.  I will post an update once the move occurs.  I hope the movers will treat my brother with dignity and move his items with care.  I have no reason not to believe this.

Well we got a few on Yelp and I was satisfied...but they only were on Yelp for a day or so! Yelp pulled off the positive reviews! They kept erasing them each time we had a new review. 
I will not be mentioning Yelp to any of my customers, and will not be paying Yelp to get us more through whatever means they get reviews. I have never seen such a funny system. 
But I will say however, that one of the men that worked for Yelp was very kind and I appreciated his advice on being aware of our online presence. I wish he would have warned me though that there is no other way, than paying them, to improve our online presence with Yelp.
